# Replace window.location.href with router.push in AuthRedirectHandler

## Summary
This PR replaces `window.location.href = nextParam` with Next.js `router.push(nextParam)` in the `AuthRedirectHandler` class to improve client-side navigation and resolve potential RSC (React Server Components) related issues.

## Changes Made
- **Modified `AuthRedirectHandler` class** (`src/lib/auth/auth-redirect-handler.ts`):
  - Added router property with type `ReturnType<typeof useRouter> | null`
  - Added `setRouter()` method for dependency injection
  - Updated `handleUserRegisteredRedirect()` to use `router.push()` instead of `window.location.href`
  - Added fallback to `window.location.href` when router is not available

- **Updated `AuthProvider` component** (`src/contexts/AuthProvider.tsx`):
  - Added `useRouter` import from "next/navigation"
  - Injected router instance into AuthRedirectHandler via `setRouter()` method

## Implementation Details

body:
## TL;DR
`common-utils`에 JSON Patch 적용 기능을 구현하고, 비교 함수의 옵션 지원을 강화하며, 유틸리티 함수 구조를 개선했습니다.

## 📌 주요 변경사항

### [기능 추가] JSON Patch 적용 기능 구현
- **`applyPatch` 함수 구현**: RFC 6902 표준에 따른 JSON Patch 적용 기능
  - `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy`, `test` 연산 지원
  - 배열과 객체 모두 지원하며 프로토타입 오염 방지
  - 473개의 상세한 테스트 케이스로 안정성 검증
- **핵심 헬퍼 함수들**:
  - `handleArray`: 배열 대상 패치 처리
  - `handleObject`: 객체 대상 패치 처리 
  - `handleRootPatch`: 루트 레벨 패치 처리
  - `getArrayIndex`: 안전한 배열 인덱스 파싱

### [기능 개선] 📌 비교(Compare) 함수 옵션 강화
- **`CompareOptions` 타입 도입**: `strict` 모드와 `immutable` 모드 지원
  - `strict: true`: 엄격한 타입 비교 (타입이 다르면 바로 다른 것으로 판단)
  - `immutable: true`: 불변 객체 처리 최적화
- **567개의 immutable 테스트**와 **834개의 strict 테스트** 추가
- **기존 235개 테스트 업데이트**하여 새로운 옵션 구조에 맞춤

### [리팩터링] 📌 구조 개선 및 정리
- **디렉토리명 통일**: `manipulators` → `manipulator`로 변경
- **patch 관련 코드 재구성**: 
  - `compare` 기능을 `patch/compare`로 이동
  - 관련 기능들을 논리적으로 그룹화
- **타입 정의 개선**: JSON Pointer 관련 타입들을 `patch/type.ts`로 통합

### [성능] 벤치마크 및 최적화
- **비교 성능 벤치마크 추가**: JSON 연산들의 성능 측정
- **Fast comparison 함수** 추가로 성능 개선

### [유지보수] 의존성 및 안정성
- **의존성 업데이트**: 안정성 향상을 위한 패키지 업데이트
- **불필요한 파일 제거**: `cloneObject.ts`, `type.ts` 등 미사용 파일 정리

## 📊 변경 통계
- **40개 파일 변경**
- **+2,552줄 추가, -391줄 삭제**
- **새로운 테스트: 1,874개** (기존 235개 + 신규 1,639개)

## 🔄 Migration Guide
기존 `compare` 함수 사용자는 다음과 같이 업데이트할 수 있습니다:

```typescript
// Before
import { compare } from '@winglet/common-utils';
const result = compare(a, b);

// After (동일한 동작)
import { compare } from '@winglet/common-utils';
const result = compare(a, b); // 기본 옵션으로 동작

// New options
const strictResult = compare(a, b, { strict: true });
const immutableResult = compare(a, b, { immutable: true });
```

---

Closes #202

body:
I've been missing the ability to track Cainiao (Aliexpress) parcels on this app which held me off from deleting my other parcel tracking app, so thought I'd have a look at adding it. Turns out it isn't that difficult!

Summary of changes:
- Added new delivery service for Cainiao deliveries in CainiaoDeliveryService.kt
- Added it to the Services enum and getDeliveryService in Core.kt
- Added a new status for when items have cleared customs but not left it yet. I don't know if you've already decided against this before so happy to remove it if you want but though I'd add it as it's a bit more clear than just 'In transit'.
- Updated readme to include Cainiao as a supported service.

I couldn't come up with any tests for this one as it seems that the tracking number can take a few formats based on the local delivery service used when the parcel arrives in the destination country, and I only have a few tracking numbers to test with from my own parcels. It will detect invalid codes in the app just fine by checking it with the API, though.

I gathered together any status codes I could find from my tracking codes and what I could find on the Aliexpress subreddit, I think most of them are covered but there may be a few uncommon ones that I didn't get. Its a bit difficult since there is no documentation for this api.

## 🎯 Problem Solved
Fixed 404 errors for images, fonts, and static assets when deploying to Vercel due to hardcoded `/AlgorithmVisualizer/` paths.

## 🔧 Changes Made

### 1. **Enhanced Next.js Configuration** (`next.config.mjs`)
- Added environment-aware deployment detection
- Conditionally applies GitHub Pages settings only when `GITHUB_PAGES=true`
- Enables clean deployment to Vercel without manual configuration

### 2. **Dynamic Asset Path Utility** (`src/lib/utils.js`)
- Created `getAssetPath()` function for environment-based path resolution
- Automatically handles path prefixes based on deployment context
- Eliminates hardcoded paths throughout the application

### 3. **Updated Components for Dynamic Paths**
- **Algorithm Cards** (`src/app/components/algorithm-cards.jsx`): Removed hardcoded paths, now uses `getAssetPath()`
- **Hero Component** (`src/app/components/hero.jsx`): Updated main hero image path
- **N-Queen Cell** (`src/app/n-queen/cell.jsx`): Fixed queen piece image loading

## ✨ Benefits
- ✅ **Vercel Ready**: All assets load correctly on Vercel deployment
- ✅ **GitHub Pages Compatible**: Maintains backward compatibility
- ✅ **Clean Codebase**: No more hardcoded paths
- ✅ **Environment Agnostic**: Works across all deployment platforms

## 🚀 Result
The algorithm visualizer now displays all images, fonts, and design elements correctly on Vercel while maintaining GitHub Pages functionality.

author: iheme01
body:
Enhanced Multi-User Storage Smart Contract

A comprehensive storage solution built on the Stacks blockchain that provides multi-user data storage with advanced features including premium subscriptions, access controls, and analytics.

Features

Core Storage Types

  • Numbers: Store unsigned integers
  • Strings: Store ASCII strings up to 256 characters
  • Booleans: Store true/false values
  • Metadata: Automatic tracking of creation time, updates, and access counts

Premium Features

  • Bulk Operations: Store multiple values at once
  • Extended Storage: Increased storage limits for premium users
  • Data Export: Export all user data in structured format
  • Data Backup: Backup data to alternate addresses
  • Advanced Search: Search functionality across stored data

Access Control

  • Public Profiles: Make your data publicly readable
  • Authorized Readers: Grant specific users access to your private data
  • Permission System: Granular control over who can access what data

Analytics & Monitoring

  • Usage Tracking: Monitor access counts and usage patterns
  • Contract Statistics: View total users, operations, and contract metrics
  • Event Logging: Comprehensive logging of all contract interactions

Contract Constants

STORAGE-FEE: 1000 microSTX (fee for premium features)
MAX-AUTHORIZED-READERS: 50 per user
MAX-STRING-LENGTH: 256 characters
BULK-OPERATION-LIMIT: 10 items per transaction

Getting Started

Basic Storage Operations

Store Data

;; Store a number
(contract-call? .storage-contract store-number u12345)

;; Store a string
(contract-call? .storage-contract store-string "Hello World")

;; Store a boolean
(contract-call? .storage-contract store-boolean true)

Retrieve Data

;; Get your own number
(contract-call? .storage-contract get-number tx-sender)

;; Get another user's public data
(contract-call? .storage-contract get-string 'ST1HTBVD3JG9C05J7HBJTHGR0GGW7KXW28M5JS8QE)

;; Get all data at once
(contract-call? .storage-contract get-all-data tx-sender)

Access Control

Make Your Profile Public

(contract-call? .storage-contract set-public-profile true)

Authorize Specific Readers

;; Allow a specific address to read your private data
(contract-call? .storage-contract add-authorized-reader 'ST1HTBVD3JG9C05J7HBJTHGR0GGW7KXW28M5JS8QE)

;; Remove authorization (simplified implementation)
(contract-call? .storage-contract remove-authorized-reader 'ST1HTBVD3JG9C05J7HBJTHGR0GGW7KXW28M5JS8QE)

Premium Features

Upgrade to Premium

;; Upgrade for 1000 blocks (duration in blocks)
(contract-call? .storage-contract upgrade-to-premium u1000)

Premium-Only Functions

;; Bulk store multiple numbers (premium only)
(contract-call? .storage-contract bulk-store-numbers (list u1 u2 u3 u4 u5))

;; Export all your data (premium only)
(contract-call? .storage-contract export-my-data)

;; Backup data to another address (premium only)
(contract-call? .storage-contract backup-data-to 'ST1BACKUP-ADDRESS)

Data Privacy & Access Rules

Who Can Read Your Data?

  1. You: Always have full access to your own data
  2. Public Profile: If enabled, anyone can read your data
  3. Authorized Readers: Users you've specifically granted access
  4. Private by Default: All data is private unless explicitly made public

Access Tracking

The contract automatically tracks:

  • When data was created and last updated
  • How many times your data has been accessed
  • Premium status and expiration
  • Total operations performed

Contract Statistics

View real-time contract metrics:

(contract-call? .storage-contract get-contract-stats)

Returns:

  • Total number of users
  • Total operations performed
  • Current contract balance
  • Current block height

Data Management

Clear All Data

;; Permanently delete all your stored data
(contract-call? .storage-contract clear-all-data)

Access with Tracking

Use these functions to access data while incrementing access counters:

(contract-call? .storage-contract access-number 'ST1USER-ADDRESS)
(contract-call? .storage-contract access-string 'ST1USER-ADDRESS)
(contract-call? .storage-contract access-boolean 'ST1USER-ADDRESS)

Error Codes

Code | Constant | Description -- | -- | -- 400 | ERR-INVALID-INPUT | Invalid input parameters 401 | ERR-UNAUTHORIZED | Insufficient permissions 402 | ERR-INSUFFICIENT-BALANCE | Not enough STX for premium features 404 | ERR-NOT-FOUND | Requested data not found 409 | ERR-ALREADY-EXISTS | Resource already exists

Premium Pricing

  • Base Fee: 1,000 microSTX per block of premium access
  • Duration: Specified in blocks (approximately 10 minutes per block)
  • Example: 144 blocks ≈ 1 day of premium access

Event Logging

The contract logs all major operations:

  • STORE_NUMBER, STORE_STRING, STORE_BOOLEAN
  • PREMIUM_UPGRADE
  • PROFILE_VISIBILITY
  • READER_ADDED, READER_REMOVED
  • BULK_STORE
  • DATA_CLEARED, DATA_BACKUP

Limitations & Notes

Current Implementation Limitations

  • User search functionality returns empty results (requires user registry)
  • Bulk operations limited to 10 items per transaction
  • Reader removal is simplified (deletes entire reader list)
  • Principal-to-string conversion is simplified

Security Considerations

  • Contract owner receives all premium payments
  • Access control is enforced on read operations
  • Data is stored permanently on-chain
  • Premium features require STX payment upfront

Development & Testing

Prerequisites

  • Stacks blockchain node or testnet access
  • Clarity CLI tools
  • STX tokens for premium features

Deployment

  1. Deploy the contract to Stacks blockchain
  2. Contract owner is set to deployer address
  3. Users can immediately start storing data

Future Enhancements

Potential improvements for future versions:

  • User registry for comprehensive search functionality
  • More sophisticated reader management
  • Subscription-based premium model
  • Data encryption options
  • Cross-contract data sharing
  • Advanced analytics dashboard

# CMake Build System Refactoring

## Overview
This PR introduces a comprehensive refactoring of the CMake build system, focusing on improved modularity, platform support, and debugging capabilities.

## Key Changes

### CMake Configuration Improvements
- Streamlined and restructured `CMakeLists.txt` files across the project
- Introduced organized sections for dependencies, configurations, and platform-specific settings
- Added clear platform macros and improved parallel build support
- Enhanced project structure with better modularization for headers, sources, and IDE organization
- Updated build directories and output structure for better organization

### Third-Party Dependencies
- Added modular Assimp configuration through `assimp.cmake`
- Refined configurations for protobuf, abseil, and other third-party libraries
- Enabled essential Assimp importers/exporters while disabling unnecessary features
- Updated property settings for conditional target checks

### Debug Support
- Added configurable `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL` support across the build system
- Exposed `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL` as a configurable option in `Configuration.cmake`
- Removed hardcoded `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL` from third-party configurations
- Ensured proper propagation of debug settings through public and private definitions

## Testing
- Verified build system changes across different configurations
- Tested parallel build support
- Validated third-party library configurations
- Confirmed debug level settings are properly propagated

## Notes
- Changes maintain backward compatibility while improving build system architecture
- Build system improvements focus on maintainability and modern CMake practices
- Debug level configuration provides better control over iterator debugging

# Implement replace string function

This PR implements the `replace` string function for GlareDB, following PostgreSQL semantics.

## Changes

- **New function**: `replace(string, from, to)` that replaces all occurrences of substring `from` with substring `to`
- **PostgreSQL compatibility**: Matches PostgreSQL behavior exactly, including edge cases
- **Proper NULL handling**: Automatically handled through TernaryExecutor framework
- **Comprehensive tests**: Added SQL Logic Tests covering various scenarios

## Implementation Details

- Created `crates/glaredb_core/src/functions/scalar/builtin/string/replace.rs` with the function implementation
- Uses `TernaryExecutor` for efficient string processing with three parameters
- Handles edge case where `from` parameter is empty (returns original string unchanged)
- Registered in builtin scalar function sets for SQL availability

## Test Coverage

Added comprehensive SLT tests in `slt/standard/functions/scalar/string/replace.slt`:
- Basic replacement scenarios
- Edge cases (empty strings, no matches, complete replacement)
- NULL input handling
- Case sensitivity verification
- Table data integration tests

## Example Usage

```sql
SELECT replace('abcdefabcdef', 'cd', 'XX');
-- Returns: 'abXXefabXXef'

SELECT replace('hello world', 'l', 'L');
-- Returns: 'heLLo worLd'
```

## Verification

- ✅ Unit tests pass: `cargo test replace_cases`
- ✅ All SLT tests pass: `./scripts/run_slt_standard.sh`
- ✅ Linting passes: `cargo clippy --all --all-features -- --deny warnings`
- ✅ Code formatted: `cargo +nightly fmt`

* Introduced the `FeedbackStatusEnum` model to support status handling for training session feedback.#

author: piotrkwarcinski
body:
### Motivation

Currently the user has an ability to go only to the previous search (`C-Enter`) with no way of going further backwards in the search history.

### Summary

* Added bindings for the search history navigation. The bindings are only a suggestion that makes sense to me, since you can navigate history in the command mode by using `C-p` and `C-n` then it would be consistent to do `C-p` and `C-n` in the search picker but as those are already taken by picker results navigation `Alt-p` and `Alt-n` make sense, as even though the modifier key changes the intent of the binding remains the same.
* If a history entry is used again then it isn't saved to the history register, this avoids inserting duplicates to the search history register when a history entry is used multiple times
* If the user navigates to a particular history entry and exits the picker then calling `Space-'` will reopen the picker at the history entry it left off.
* Added saving to the search history register on `C-v`, `C-s`, `Alt-Enter`.

author: pastapastapasta
body:
Backports bitcoin/bitcoin#26053

RPC: bugfix, 'add_inputs' default value is true unless 'inputs' are provided

In both RPC commands `send()` and `walletcreatefundedpsbt` the RPC help was saying
that `add_inputs` default value was false when it's actually dynamically set
by the following statement:

`coin_control.m_add_inputs = rawTx.vin.size() == 0;`

Which means that, by default, `add_inputs` is true unless there
was any pre-set input, in which case, the default is false.

Original commit: 2e3cd26a1a5e071407b79cf02c35f6cf42aa6191

author: bufdev
body:
This promotes `buf beta stats` to `buf stats` and does a few cleanups along the way:

- The `num` prefix is removed from the `protostats.Stats` type and from the JSON output.
- The text output is moved from a two-row tab printout, to a newline printout.
- The concept of `Types` is added, since this is the most common use case for stats.
- `Methods` is renamed to `RPCs`, which is how most people understand this.
- `FilesWithSyntaxErrors` is no longer reported, as no one really cares except us.

author: trainzluvr
body:
tldr;

In process_data(), we call notify_empty() which resets countL_ and countH_ as well as currentAddress_ to 0. This affects operation of the Railcom hardware channel 0 when DCC timer tick is tied to the same hardware channel, causing the failure to process Railcom data.

The long

On LCC nodes that detect Railcom data, physical ports enumerate from 0. The DCC timer tick also happens to be tied to hardware channel 0 at least in one implementation (Tiva Railcom/openmrn_cue) where empty Railcom ch1 and ch2 packets are constantly being sent, and eventually reaching RailcomBroadcastDecoder.cxx

These packets marked as coming from hardware channel 0 end up resetting the countL_/countH_/currentAddress_ because they pass through process_data() method and being empty (packet.ch1Size is false) hit notify_empty().

The flood of these empty packets is what causes the reset (the DCC timer tick happens more frequently) while the actual Railcom data from hardware channel 0 never gets to be processed - we require countL_ and countH_ both to be >= MIN_REPEAT_COUNT * 2, but notify_empty() gets called on every DCC timer tick never allowing the counters to increase.

This is only the case with hardware channel 0. All other hardware channels are not impacted, neither by the DCC timer tick (when bound to hardware channel 0) nor by removal of notify_empty() from the process_data() method.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The `safeJsonParse` function in `jsonUtils.ts` was calling `.trim()` on database values without checking if they were strings first. When the database returned NULL values, numbers, booleans, or other non-string types, this caused a critical error:

```
Error getting player: TypeError: jsonString.trim is not a function
```

This broke all player-related functionality:
- Players couldn't use `/status` (says they're not a player)
- Players couldn't use `/join` (gets multiple errors)
- Database constraint violations from failed player lookups
- The bot was essentially non-functional for gameplay

## Root Cause

The issue was in this line in `safeJsonParse`:
```typescript
if (!jsonString || jsonString.trim() === '') {
```

While the parameter was typed as `string | null | undefined`, the database could actually return any type, and calling `.trim()` on a non-string value throws a TypeError.

## Solution

Added a type check before calling `.trim()`:

```typescript
export function safeJsonParse<T>(
  jsonString: any,
  fallback: T,
  context?: string
): SafeJsonParseResult<T> {
  // Handle non-string inputs
  if (typeof jsonString !== 'string') {
    return {
      success: true,
      data: fallback
    };
  }

  // Handle empty or whitespace-only strings
  if (!jsonString || jsonString.trim() === '') {
    return {
      success: true,
      data: fallback
    };
  }
  
  // ... rest of function
}
```

## Changes Made

1. **Added type check** in `safeJsonParse` to handle non-string inputs gracefully
2. **Updated function signature** to accept `any` type instead of `string | null | undefined`
3. **Updated `safeJsonParseArray`** to match the new signature
4. **Added comprehensive tests** covering number, boolean, object, and null inputs
5. **Enhanced edge case tests** specifically for database scenarios

## Testing

Added tests that verify the fix handles all problematic database value types:
- Numbers: `123` → returns fallback without error
- Booleans: `true` → returns fallback without error  
- Objects: `{ some: 'object' }` → returns fallback without error
- Null/undefined: properly handled as before

All existing functionality is preserved with zero breaking changes.

## Impact

This minimal change restores critical game functionality:
- ✅ Players can now use `/status` command successfully
- ✅ Players can now use `/join` command without errors
- ✅ Player retrieval from database works correctly
- ✅ No more database constraint violations from failed lookups

Fixes #101.

author: apo-mak
body:
This pull request introduces support for Greek (`el`) language responses, intents, and test cases for the `HassGetCurrentDate` and `HassGetCurrentTime` functionalities. The changes include the addition of localized response templates, intent definitions, and corresponding test cases.

### Greek Language Support for Date and Time Intents:

#### Response Templates:
* Added Greek-language response template for `HassGetCurrentDate`, which formats the date using Greek month names. (`responses/el/HassGetCurrentDate.yaml`)
* Added Greek-language response template for `HassGetCurrentTime`, which formats the time in 24-hour format with leading zeros. (`responses/el/HassGetCurrentTime.yaml`)

#### Intent Definitions:
* Defined Greek-language sentences for `HassGetCurrentDate` intent, covering various ways users might ask for the current date. (`sentences/el/homeassistant_HassGetCurrentDate.yaml`)
* Defined Greek-language sentences for `HassGetCurrentTime` intent, covering various ways users might ask for the current time. (`sentences/el/homeassistant_HassGetCurrentTime.yaml`)

#### Test Cases:
* Added test cases for `HassGetCurrentDate` in Greek, ensuring the intent correctly maps to the response "17 Σεπτεμβρίου 2013" for various input sentences. (`tests/el/homeassistant_HassGetCurrentDate.yaml`)
* Added test cases for `HassGetCurrentTime` in Greek, ensuring the intent correctly maps to the response "01:02" for various input sentences. (`tests/el/homeassistant_HassGetCurrentTime.yaml`)
